newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: ADB asks Bangladesh to raise power tariff 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: ADB asks Bangladesh to raise power tariff 25 pct.

text.p: Asian Development Bank, a major donor, has warned Bangladesh that it will withdraw from funding a $300 million power project unless the country raises its electricity tariff by 25 percent, The Daily Star said on Tuesday.

The newspaper said the Manila-based bank was to offer Bangladesh $100 million in credit. The other financiers are World Bank and the British government. The project aims to improve power distribution system, it said.

The Daily Star quoted officials as saying that the government at a meeting with ADB officials on Monday refused to make a sharp hike in the tariff but agreed on a maximum 15 percent rise in phases. Bangladesh has not raised power rates since 1991.
The ADB is insisting on the privatisation of the Dhaka Electric Supply Authority (DESA) to reduce the wastage and theft of electricity, currently running upto 37 percent, the paper said.
